items.title: Iron Mountain Raises Its Dividend 15% as Data Center Revenue Surges 34%
items.summary: A company famous for storing paper boxes now funds its shareholder payouts with server halls. Income investors should weigh how Iron Mountain stacks up against Digital Realty and Equinix, and which balance sheet figure could complicate the story.

items.title: Iron Mountain Q3 Earnings Call Highlights

The company also increased its quarterly dividend by 15%. Revenue rose 13% from a year earlier to $1.99 bil

items.title: What Is Behind Iron Mountain (IRM) Raising Its Dividend By 15%?
items.summary: Iron Mountain (NYSE:IRM) increased its quarterly dividend by 15%, highlighting management confidence in the business on 6 November 2026. The higher payout follows a recent quarter in which Iron Mountain reported record revenue levels for the group. Management linked the larger dividend to expectations for stronger adjusted funds from operations and a constructive outlook for 2026. The 15% dividend lift is important, but there is more to Iron Mountain's income story than this single move...
